key_insight: Train the LLM at test time with reinforcement learning so it adapts to the specific problem instance and iteratively discovers a single, superior solution rather than relying on frozen prompting or averaging many outputs.
problem_solved: How to push a model to discover a new state-of-the-art solution for a specific scientific/test problem by continuing to learn from experience during inference, instead of using a frozen model or search over prompts.
method: Run reinforcement learning during inference: generate candidate solutions, evaluate them against the task objective, and update the model policy using the feedback.
Optimize for a single-best outcome (continual/test-time learning) rather than average-case performance, enabling aggressive exploration-exploitation tailored to the current test instance.
Contrast with prior test-time search (e.g., prompting a frozen LLM): incorporate on-the-fly parameter updates so the model accumulates problem-specific experience.
impact: Enables automated discovery of higher-quality, instance-specific solutions (useful for scientific tasks, optimization, and benchmarks) by allowing models to adapt and improve at test time rather than relying on static inference strategies.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic: Frozen prompt-based search (multiple static outputs) vs. Test-time RL loop (generate → evaluate → update → repeat).
Flowchart of the test-time RL cycle showing candidate generation, evaluation metric, reward signal, and policy update step.
Performance curve showing single-run improvement over iterations (score vs. inference steps) compared to baseline frozen LLM.
Icon set: magnifying glass for discovery, lightning bolt for rapid adaptation, and trophy for new state-of-the-art.
paper_title: Learning to Discover at Test Time
paper_authors: Mert Yuksekgonul, Daniel Koceja, Xinhao Li, Federico Bianchi, Jed McCaleb
